speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head N of the Estimates be reduced by $100." In 1945, following the end of World War II, the countries of the world came together to set up the United Nations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The leaders behind this initiative included the US, the Soviet Union, the Republic of China, the United Kingdom and France, the five permanent members of the Security Council.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The same concept had been applied a year earlier in 1944 at Bretton Woods when the world community came together to set up the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, which later became the World Bank.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: These institutions became operational in 1945, once enough countries signed up.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: After the horrors of World War II, the idea behind these international agreements was to set up systems for a multilateral world where countries could mutually benefit and prosper.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The UN would facilitate collective action in relation to security matters.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The IMF would help regulate financial and currency markets; the World Bank would provide loans, initially, to help reconstruct countries ravaged by the war, but later, to help developing countries in need; and GATT, which laid the foundation for world trade, was to help countries prosper through international trade.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: On the back of these organisations, many countries, Singapore included, lived in a world that was relatively safe and provided the means for any country big or small to prosper and develop.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Of course, there was no panacea to eliminate conflict altogether and poverty.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But, certainly, as a whole, the end of World War II has marked a heightened awareness and compliance with these international norms than any century before.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Against this backdrop, the events in recent years have marked strong pressures amongst nations to pull back from multilateralism.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The fast-moving business cycles and dynamism of creative destruction have left many workers in countries feeling displaced as the companies they worked in were restructured or disrupted.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: At the same time, those who did the disruption profited handsomely, with fresh billionaires being minted every year, particularly in the technology sector.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Free trade has been under continuing pressure, with the two largest economies, China and the US, having an intense rivalry in recent years that has made both more insular with their economic focus.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The multilateral response to uphold the prohibition against the use of force is also under intense pressure.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It would be possible for countries to take action outside the auspices of the UN, say, if they were invited by Ukraine's government to assist.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But other countries, including those in NATO, have been reluctant to get involved militarily as they are concerned this may escalate matters into a full-blown European war.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: As a result, Ukraine has been left to fight the war on its own.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The weakening of this multilateral system is a serious concern for me, particularly where it appears to be that the major powers who were the architects of the system are themselves pulling away from it.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This makes it more likely that major powers will clash and that smaller countries may get swallowed up or trampled on during these confrontations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: What is Singapore's best approach in such an environment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In an increasingly polarised world, we have also seen major powers manoeuvring and wielding disproportionate influence at such multilateral platforms.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Why does Singapore continue to place a heavy emphasis on multilateralism?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Should we instead channel our efforts and resources more to bilateral and regional forums like the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) and so on where we can better galvanise actions and make real impact?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: The weakening of people-to-people linkages between the US and China amid the COVID-19 pandemic has not helped.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Both superpowers are also trying to strengthen their engagement of our region through their multilateral initiatives, such as the US' Free and Open Indo-Pacific Strategy and China's Belt and Road Initiative.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: We have seen this new political tussle between the US and China played out on the global stage and closer to home, in the South China Sea and during ASEAN meetings.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: This tension was also felt at non-political events, such as the Summit for Democracy, by which countries were invited by the US, and the diplomatic boycotts of the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics and Paralympic Games.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Singapore enjoys close ties with both the US and China.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: We welcomed US Vice-President Kamala Harris to Singapore in August 2021, while President Halimah Yacob visited Beijing just last month.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Singapore's defence relationship with the US is underpinned by milestone bilateral agreements, such as the 1990 MOU regarding the US' use of facilities in Singapore, which was renewed during Prime Minister Lee's visit to the US in September 2019.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Chairman, over the last two years, the pandemic has changed the way we live and travel.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: When COVID-19 first broke out two years ago, we had many Singaporeans abroad who wanted to return, at a time when flights and travel were high-risk activities, and those returning Singaporeans also posed the risk of bringing COVID-19 home when they returned.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: More recently, when flights to many countries resumed, including the Vaccinated Travel Lane (VTL) and shorter quarantine periods, Singaporeans resumed travel and I expect a number would have captured COVID-19 overseas.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I myself mentioned earlier that I was part of this statistic when my family travelled to London and both my daughter and I tested positive.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But my own experience with the High Commission in London was very positive and I am grateful for the assistance they rendered to help us navigate what needed to be done.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Looking at the statistics, the number of people getting COVID-19, I can imagine there are likely to be many other Singaporeans who are getting COVID-19 abroad.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: In this regard, I would like to ask what was MFA's role like during the pandemic and whether its policy priorities have changed.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I was hoping that COVID-19, like SARS, would go away after a few months.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, this seems to be far from the case.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Part of the reason may be the fact that we are now a more connected world and people who travel between countries are the norm.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many of my residents were affected by the restrictions imposed on them or their relatives due to COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Children studying overseas had to disrupt their studies to either come back or they had to make a decision to remain out of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Those residents with business interests overseas were also adversely affected as they cannot travel to their offices or factories in other countries.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Are we in a position to help other countries with surgical masks, sanitisers, vaccines or even test kits in order to build on our relationship with other countries?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As a small nation, we need to remain relevant and to have more friends.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, as a small country that must navigate various forces, we must be wary of not just traditional geopolitical realities, but new and non-traditional challenges.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Besides cybersecurity and climate change, what are some emerging and salient issues that are currently discussed at multilateral fora and how is Singapore addressing them?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For example, interconnectedness through increased globalisation has reshaped threats to the modern state, such as terrorist groups, piracy networks and other non-state actions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We no longer just have a singular focus on military affairs, but we need to also think about non-military threats and also from the rise of non-state groups.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Dealing with such threats and risks requires diplomacy and non-military responses.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Living through a pandemic today on an island that is vulnerable to rising sea levels as our climate changes, importing all our energy needs, we are a young nation, porous to overseas values and cultural debates which may fracture our historical fault lines.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Paying close attention to such issues translates into the way we manage social and moral issues, such as equality and race relations, as well as more pragmatic ones, such as supplies of food and vaccines.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Let us not take for granted that as a small country with little geopolitical weight, we were one of the earliest to secure vaccines for everyone living on this island.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Chairman, I had filed this cut prior to the Russian invasion to ask for MFA's response in relation to the situation in Ukraine.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Since then, the invasion has taken place and I think the Minister has made Singapore's position clear in the Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I do have a few related questions, though.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: As we speak, the fighting is still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: According to reports, Ukraine is significantly outnumbered by Russia's military and military resources, but they have been putting up fierce resistance.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It is not clear how long Ukraine will be able to hold out for or how long this conflict will last.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: There has been news coverage, both of Ukrainians in Singapore, as well as Singaporeans in Ukraine.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: The destruction and loss of innocent lives caused by the invasion of Ukraine by Russia are simply unacceptable as this is a blatant interference with the sovereignty of another country.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan had issued a Ministerial Statement about the Ukraine situation on Monday.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I agree and fully support the stand taken by the Singapore Government.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: As a small country, we have to insist on the principles of respect for national sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity and also on the rule of law.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: What else can we do to promote peace between our neighbours?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: What else can we do to provide support to the people of Ukraine?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the global order, small states have little intrinsic relevance.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the face of regional and global geopolitical developments, small states are often price takers.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In many ways, 24 February this year will go down in the history books as the day history repeats itself.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As curtains to the full-on military conflict in Ukraine were raised, what George Bernard Shaw said that "We learn from history that we learn nothing from history" takes on fresh relevance.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan has delivered a Ministerial Statement on Monday explaining our response and sanctions on Russia.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I fully agree with the Minister when he says that this crisis is of existential concern to small states like Singapore.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: International law and principles enshrined in the UN Charter must be upheld.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We should avoid getting ourselves caught up in geopolitical games.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Internally, we must be united and, at the same time, always stand ready to stand for our interests and our sovereignty.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Like many Singaporeans, I watch the daily developments in Ukraine with much unease.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While the conflict in Ukraine remains somewhat a distant theatre of operations, what can we do to be sure that Singapore and Singaporeans really pick up and internalise relevant lessons because those who fail to learn from history are doomed to repeat it?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Chairman, our bilateral relations with our Southeast Asian (SEA) neighbours, as well as their relations with one another, are of paramount importance to us.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Given the importance of our immediate region, can MFA provide an update on our relations with our Southeast Asian neighbours?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, Malaysia is one of Singapore’s closest neighbours.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Most of us have friends and loved ones on both sides of the Causeway and, prior to the pandemic, had often travelled to each other’s country for leisure and work.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have cooperated closely in many areas, including trade and investment, maritime security and environmental protection.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Singapore and Malaysia are each other’s second most important trading partners.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has severely impacted travel arrangements as well as other projects and engagements.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: What are some initiatives we can expect to see rolled out this year following the above two MOUs?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: And how will Singapore continue to work with Indonesia to strengthen bilateral cooperation, including at the central and regional levels, following the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders’ Retreat held in Bintan on 25 January 2022?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our relations with Brunei have been very close and mutually beneficial for many years.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In 2021, Brunei assumed the chairmanship of ASEAN in the midst of great challenges brought upon by the COVID-19 pandemic in Southeast Asia and other issues as well, such as the military coup in Myanmar and the ongoing maritime disputes in the South China Sea.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: ASEAN, under the chairmanship of Brunei, would have to cooperate, navigate and chart a post-pandemic future together to achieve stability and prosperity in the region.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this regard, can the Minister please elaborate on how we have maintained our excellent relations with Brunei in the midst of these challenges?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And what are the highlights of Brunei's chairmanship of ASEAN in 2021?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: It was not how the concept of ASEAN was originally founded on where the grouping's role is meant to be limited, with a strong adherence to the principle of non-interference in each member state's internal affairs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: ASEAN has strengthened its engagement with external partners over the years with the setting up of extra-regional platforms such as, ASEAN Plus Three, ASEAN Regional Forums, ASEAN Defence Ministers Plus, Extended ASEAN Maritime Forum, to name a few.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The engagement agenda has also gotten more substantial and taken on a more ASEAN-centric stand to regional or global issues.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can I seek an update from the Minister on how Singapore will continue to play its part in maintaining ASEAN's centrality, unity and credibility?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Chairman, the unending civil war in Myanmar is nothing short of a humanitarian disaster.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Singaporeans are rightfully concerned because of our relationships with the people of Myanmar and our business ties with Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: At the same time, how ASEAN responds to the civil war in Myanmar is also a major test for ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: ASEAN countries will need to balance our deeply-held belief of non-interference in the affairs of member states, with our natural instincts of encouraging conditions of peace and stability not just among ASEAN nations, but also within ASEAN nations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: As such, can MFA provide an update on the ASEAN response to Myanmar?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Chairman, our leaders had a series of high-level exchanges with their counterparts from the Middle East, particularly the Gulf countries, recently.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Education Mohamad Maliki Osman visited the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Qatar and Saudi Arabia to engage their political leaders in October last year.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: In mid-January this year, Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister His Highness Prince Faisal Bin Farhan Al Saud visited Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: A few days later, our Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu visited the UAE to attend the Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: This was shortly followed by Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security Teo Chee Hean’s visit to the UAE to officiate the Singapore Day ceremony at Expo 2020 Dubai.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: He also met the leaders of Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Would the Ministry share how Singapore is maintaining its relations with the Gulf countries, considering the impact of the pandemic?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: How have Singapore’s relations with the Gulf countries developed given the recent visits to and from the region?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: (In Malay):   Since last August, Saudi Arabia has welcomed international vaccinated Umrah pilgrims, after a gap of one and a half years due to COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: In fact, many Singaporeans performed their Umrah during this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: As Umrah for international pilgrims has resumed since last August, could we expect the Haj to resume for Singapore pilgrims for this year, too?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: In last August too, I asked a Parliamentary Question during the tensions in Palestine.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Can the Minister for Foreign Affairs update us on efforts to support capacity building in the Palestinian Authority?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Chairman, beyond our relationship with the US and China, it is also important that Singapore continues to strengthen its global network of friends.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In light of the tension between the US and China, what more can we do to strengthen this network and enhance these partnerships with other key partners?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Chairman, the US has been an important power in the world and the region since World War II.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The US was a reluctant entrant in that war, but its entry into the war was definitive in the Pacific theatre.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Since then, whenever there have been violations of Article 24 of the UN Charter, the US has played, again, a decisive role in these matters, including in the invasion of Kuwait.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: More recently, though, the US seems to be heavily preoccupied with internal matters, particularly with the mid-term elections coming in November and it looks like control of both Houses may be in the balance.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Are there any steps that we can take to continue to engage the US and to keep them involved and interested in the region?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore and the US have been close partners in support of the rules-based economic and security order within our region since our Independence.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The US is also Singapore’s top trading partner in services and Singapore’s third largest partner in merchandise trade.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The most recent development is on the proposed Indo-Pacific Economic Framework put forward by the Biden administration.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While still light on details, a White House factsheet on the Indo-Pacific Strategy of the US gives us insights on the areas of engagement, including labour and environmental standards, a new digital economy framework, building resilient and secure supply chains, and making shared investments in decarbonisation and clean energy.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If actualised, the plan presents significant opportunities for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: One that comes to mind is the question of US commitment.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The domestic political atmosphere in the US is one that is sceptical of trade and other economic deals that are perceived to place American businesses and workers at a disadvantage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Such conditions are apparent across the political spectrum.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This could affect the degree of US commitment to the framework.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: There may also be concerns in Beijing that Singapore may be cooperating in an effort that undermines Chinese interests.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Such considerations may be especially important, given the current heightened levels of suspicion and competition between the US and China.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Beyond navigating ties between the US and China, how will Singapore balance joining the Framework and fit in with various other economic arrangements which Singapore is currently committed to?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would, therefore, like to ask the Minister how does Singapore plan to engage with the US under this Indo-Pacific Economic Framework.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, Singapore has had a long and cordial relationship with China.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have been cooperating in many areas, including investment and trading, and have deep and robust ties through our joint entities and our people.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Quite a number of Singaporeans and Chinese also share family ties.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Both countries are committed to the many growing areas of cooperation and it can be seen in how both established a fast lane in early June 2020 to facilitate essential business and official travel.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is significant because the fast lane was China’s first with a Southeast Asian country.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore has enjoyed good relations with Japan and South Korea as well.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many Japanese and Korean companies have made investments and set up offices in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singaporeans are very familiar with Japanese and South Korean products, entertainment and cultural influence.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Japan and South Korea have been two of the most popular travel destinations among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are many Japanese and Korean families living and working here as well.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What steps have we taken to broaden our bilateral ties and strengthen our cooperation with China, Japan and the Republic of Korea amidst the pandemic?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will these ties translate into cooperation in technological and business development on the ground for the benefit of all parties?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Chairman, we have had a strong relationship with India over the years.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Historically, it was India's independence that paved the way for many former colonies of the United Kingdom, including Singapore, to also become independent, in the post-war wave of decolonisation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: In more recent years, ties have been strong between India and Singapore with multiple top-level meetings taking place between Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Relations have been cemented with the Singapore-India Strategic Partnership signed during Prime Minister Modi's visit to Singapore in 2015 and updated in 2017 and 2018.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: There were several high-level, Ministerial visits taking place between the countries during 2018 and 2019 as well prior to the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Over the last two years, though, actual visits have been difficult.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They noted the good progress made in the Singapore-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) over the past year despite challenges presented by COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The Prime Ministers also agreed to keep the CSP forward-looking by furthering cooperation in emerging areas such as low-emissions solutions and fintech.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This arrangement enabled both countries to support each other in optimising our respective schedules for vaccinating our populations against COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Since November 2021, fully vaccinated Singapore Citizens have been able to travel to most Australian cities quarantine-free.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is much welcomed news for many Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Another Oceania country we have close relations with is New Zealand.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We share many interests and strategic views and cooperate closely both bilaterally and multilaterally.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: When the pandemic struck, Singapore and New Zealand reaffirmed our commitment to maintaining trade flows for essential goods by co-sponsoring the Joint Statement on Open Markets, Flow of Essential Goods and Supply Chain Connectivity issued by the UN in May 2020.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are great opportunities for Singapore with these two countries.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, thank you for the privilege to participate in this debate.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Earlier in the week, Minister for Foreign Affairs Vivian Balakrishnan gave this House an insightful and heart-wrenching Ministerial Statement on the situation in Ukraine and its implications.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans must not think that it can never happen to us.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: As I said in my Budget debate speech, Singapore's Total Defence along with our diplomatic corps cannot be over-emphasised.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans cannot take our existence as a nation for granted.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We must do our best not to be taken for granted by others.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, let me start by sharing three reflections.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: My first reflection is that our Singapore voice must be heard clearly but humbly.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore is a small country and a young nation in a big world.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: In global geopolitics, it is paramount that we develop and maintain strong diplomatic relations with everyone without compromising our independence, values and principles.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: It is pertinent, therefore, that our Singapore voice be heard clearly but humbly.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We must have the courage to speak and act with integrity to protect the sovereignty of our country.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: If you heard Singapore's Permanent Representative Burhan Gafoor take the stage as last speaker at the UN General Assembly's special emergency session to present Singapore's view, that is our collective courage.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: That takes me to my second reflection: Singapore must not be used by anyone.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The terrorists in Ukraine should remind us of the dangers of division and fragmentation of a society, falling prey to foreign influence or foreign might.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We must never be the vassal state of any other power.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: My third reflection is that even though we are small, Singapore and Singaporeans can play our part as channels of peace, dialogue and reconciliation.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, we live in an increasingly polarised and uncertain world.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The strategic competition between the US and China has widened and deepened, pulling other countries into the fray.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We have seen this playing out in fields such as the deployment of 5G networks.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: There is also growing talk of a new cold war in Europe arising from the tragic situation in Ukraine, invoking the imagery of opposing ideologies that cannot be reconciled.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Closer to home, the situation in Myanmar continues to be a challenge for ASEAN.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: These developments have and will continue to have significant geopolitical and economic ramifications on all countries, including Singapore.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Amidst these challenges, how does Singapore continue to maintain an independent foreign policy and how do we balance between being your brother's keeper and minding your own business when it comes to diplomacy?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For fellow Singaporeans living away from home, MFA's overseas missions are their primary point of contact when they require any assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Now, consular assistance does not affect most Singaporean travelers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, the pandemic has highlighted the importance of MFA's consular assistance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I wish to thank our MFA officers for working round the clock to serve our fellow residents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In particular, some of the officers have not been home since the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Their dedication and commitment in serving our fellow citizens abroad are commendable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In addition to the rapidly evolving COVID-19 situation, we are now facing an uncertain global security climate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Could MFA update on its efforts to improve the delivery of consular assistance to Singaporeans overseas?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Is there a need for MFA to establish ground presence in more countries?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How about the support to Singaporeans affected by the Ukrainian-Russian conflict?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Furthermore, despite international borders reopening, there are still a few countries that remain closed to international travellers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How would MFA assist Singaporeans who need to travel to these countries for compassionate reasons amidst the pandemic?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mr Chairman, we live in an increasingly uncertain world.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The strategic competition between the US and China has intensified.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Other countries have inevitably found themselves drawn into it and found themselves confronted with difficult choices.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Countries are also grappling with global issues such as supply chain disruptions, technology bifurcation and climate change and the impact these have on their peoples and economies.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singapore has to respond to these fast-changing developments and make very difficult choices as well and we need Singaporeans to believe and understand that our chosen courses of action are taken after very careful consideration in their best interests.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But the considerations that drive our decision making on foreign policy issues are complex and often hard to understand or translate into layman's terms.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry share what it is doing to deepen Singaporeans' understanding of the key tenets of our foreign policy and the considerations for them?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can foreign policy issues be made easy for the man in the street to understand?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we highlight the ways in which good foreign policy contributes to the well-being of Singapore and Singaporeans and get domestic support for our foreign policy decisions?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is extremely important because the understanding will help build trust between the Government and the people.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The unity gives us a strong coherent voice in our interactions with foreign countries.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Minister consider providing easy-to-read information to schools, tertiary institutions, grassroots, community partners and even religious organisations?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Chairman, it has been a very busy year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As always, we are trying to secure our place in a very volatile and, I would say, dangerous world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The key issues confronting us are: first, COVID-19 and its aftermath; second, navigating major power rivalry, fostering peace, upholding international law, strengthening multilateralism; third, protecting the global commons, including addressing non-traditional challenges; fourth, nurturing Singapore's relations with our neighbours; and fifth, ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, let me deal with COVID-19 because Mr Vikram Nair, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Lim Biow Chuan have asked how COVID-19 has affected our foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The pandemic has impacted – in fact, disrupted – the lives of many overseas Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA's duty in the last two years has been to make sure that we left no Singaporean behind.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA also supported the launch of Vaccinated Travel Lanes (VTLs) and the mutual recognition of health certificates in order to facilitate the safe resumption of international travel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore has also supported global COVID-19 vaccination – because no one is safe until everyone is safe in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have contributed to the COVAX Advance Market Commitment and the COVID-19 ASEAN Response Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I wish to commend the dedication of all MFA staff, both those serving in Singapore as well as in our Overseas Missions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Over 300 MFA officers have served Singapore at our Overseas Missions during this period and I am very proud that not a single officer has asked to leave their posts because of the risk of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Despite our best efforts and health precautions, about 40 of our officers serving overseas as well as another 150 foreigners who are employed by our Missions overseas did succumb to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But again, it is a symbol of their commitment and their willingness to sacrifice for the sake of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We owe them a big debt of gratitude.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: COVID-19 will not be the last or even the worst pandemic faced by the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we will continue to work with the international community, including and especially through the WHO, in order to strengthen the global health architecture and to enhance pandemic preparedness and resilience and the ability to cooperate as a single world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The ongoing developments in Ukraine are a stark reminder of the vulnerability of small states when confronted by a larger and more powerful opponent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Vikram Nair, Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Mr Eric Chua, Ms Janet Ang and Mr Baey Yam Keng have all asked very salient questions about multilateralism, about the world order and about big power rivalry.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In my Ministerial Statement on 28 February, I explained why we have to be such a staunch supporter of international law and the principles enshrined in the UN Charter.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must take a stand against actions that clearly violate the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of another country, of all countries, because, ultimately, this is also about us, as a tiny city state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When push comes to shove, smaller countries like Singapore must be prepared to defend ourselves and not get caught up in the geopolitical games of big powers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we do take a stand to uphold existential principles.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to try to get humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and, of course, we continue to monitor the evacuation of Singaporeans in Ukraine.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have got another further three out, and there are still six left there.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has intensified across multiple domains and, quite frankly, the strategic choices of both these countries will shape the emerging international order profoundly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Under President Biden, US foreign policy has become, in a sense, more predictable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, its fundamental approach and the policies of the US towards China have basically remained unchanged.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, the sanctions against Chinese entities have not been relaxed but have become even tougher.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both political parties in America as well as the business community and even society at large have come to, generally, view China as a direct threat to the United States' interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is compounded by the fact that the US has never, in its history, faced a peer competitor on such a scale.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On China's part, there is a growing perception that the US is a declining power reacting defensively and aggressively to China's inevitable growth and progress.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, China will want to avoid being seen to be pressured into making concessions in its policies or posture, out of a concern that any concession on its part will only lead to continued or even increased pressure from other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: US and China's relationship is fraught with many spiky issues and this is complicated by domestic considerations, and the distrust, the rivalry have intensified over the past few years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Trade and economic issues can be negotiated and compromises found.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Otherwise, it will be very difficult for them to cooperate constructively, even where their interests are aligned.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: How the US and China compete and cooperate will determine not just their trajectories, but that of the rest of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It would be disastrous for both powers to focus on what they call "extreme competition", or even outright confrontation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And the old Cold War strategy of containment will not be viable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We, therefore, welcome efforts by both the US and China to engage at the highest levels to cooperate on global challenges like climate change and the digital age, and we encourage greater people-to-people engagement as travel restrictions are removed in order to foster generations, especially younger people in both the United States and China, to understand and to appreciate each other's values, attitudes, strengths and weaknesses.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope that these interactions will encourage greater trust and pave the way forward for a more constructive relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As the former Secretary of State George Shultz wisely observed, he said – and this is worth remembering 	– "Trust is the coin of the realm.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When trust was in the room, good things happened.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When trust was not in the room, good things did not happen.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Everything else is details." On Singapore's part, we enjoy excellent ties and, in fact, I may add, high levels of trust with both the US and China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we have been able to maintain high-level interactions even amidst COVID-19 over the past two years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In 2021 alone, we welcomed visits by US Vice President Kamala Harris, Secretary of Defence Lloyd Austin, Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I also made a working visit to Washington where I met with my counterpart, Secretary of State Antony Blinken.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: President Biden will be hosting an ASEAN-US Summit in Washington later this month.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also maintained intensive engagements with our Chinese counterparts, including through mutual support when we both needed it during COVID-19 at its worst moments, as well as bilateral cooperation and at the Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation meeting co-chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat in December last year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Since 2020 – and I double-checked this number – I have met or spoken with my counterpart, State Councilor and Foreign Minister Wang Yi, on nine occasions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, that is about once every three months.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And our most recent engagement was in Beijing last month, when I accompanied President Halimah Yacob to the opening ceremony of the Beijing Winter Olympics.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And there is a standing invitation for President Halimah to make a formal State Visit to China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is in Singapore's interest to continue to foster stronger ties with both the US and China and to be a consistent and reliable partner to both for the long term.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we have not shied away from standing up for ourselves and disagreeing on issues when necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we do not have the luxury of saying different things to different partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, Singapore strives to be straightforward, consistent, reliable, trustworthy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To this end, we will also work with all parties to uphold an open, inclusive, stable, peaceful, rules-based international order.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There were questions just now about the TPP and the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework by Mr Dennis Tan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is still the highest level and most ambitious Free Trade Agreement with safeguards not only for trade, labour, the environment, intellectual property; and the rest of it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But all my interlocutors in America have said they cannot do it because of domestic political reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In a sense, the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework is an alternative which they are trying to put beef on this framework.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Let us see and let us encourage them.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But as I have said, the key point I keep making and, in fact, the Prime Minister has made to multiple Presidents in Asia, trade is strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked why Singapore continues to place such heavy emphasis on multilateralism, given that powerful states are often perceived to wield outsized influence at multinational platforms, and he asked whether we should just focus on bilateral and regional arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked how Singapore's foreign policy can remain independent while balancing and advancing our own national interests, as opposed to, and she even asked why should we be our brother's keeper.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With global economic integration and the expansion of cross-border capital and trade flows over the last century, the fortunes of all countries and all peoples are now increasingly interdependent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, multilateralism and economic integration have been a formula for peace and prosperity for many decades since the end of the last (Second) World War, and especially critical for small states like us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In today's charged geopolitical context, it is even more important that small states continue to stand up for a stronger United Nations and a robust multilateral system that levels the playing fields, takes all countries' interests into account.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These regional agreements facilitate more efficient, more diversified and resilient supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They increase access to global markets, encourage rules-based trading activity and foster greater connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Even in Singapore, as we face pushback from some people against economic integration, it is important to redouble and reaffirm that this is an essential pillar for our economic strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third, let me deal with our international work on the global commons and non-traditional security challenges that have been raised.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Countries are grappling with geopolitical flashpoints, insularism and major power politics.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng reminded us and asked about Singapore's approach to these emerging issues at multilateral fora.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Well, there is certainly no shortage of emerging non-traditional issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The ones which often come to mind are climate change, food security, emerging diseases, the challenges and problems of the digital economy and the threats in cyberspace and, eventually, and, in fact, emerging, outer space as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Again, our approach is that we believe in multilateralism and that these issues should best be pursued at multilateral fora, including the United Nations, APEC, G20 and ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Basically, an opportunity for us to work together, address the challenges, the opportunities, deal with the dangers, establish common standards, norms, rules and, ultimately, hopefully, norms for state behaviours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this is the way, in a sense, we have to protect the global commons, public health, the oceans, the environment, cyberspace, outer space.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, Singapore has a history of outsized contributions in protecting the global commons.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Climate change, we all know, is an existential threat to mankind and as a small city-state, we are exquisitely vulnerable to the impact of climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Encouraging progress was made at the most recent 26th Conference of the Parties, and I am sure Minister Grace Fu will explain.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But in case she is too humble, let me say that she and her team have continued this tradition of being excellent ministerial facilitators, being honest brokers and arriving at consensus and making progress for the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And notwithstanding our small size, our pioneers, including Ambassador-at-Large professor Prof Tommy Koh, played again an outsized role and helped to bring UNCLOS to fruition 40 years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we continue to play a constructive role in oceans-related issues and right now, Ambassador Rena Lee has been the President of the Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction Intergovernmental Conference since 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Most people may not be aware of this, but this is another offshoot of UNCLOS.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fourth, peace and stability in our immediate neighbourhood are absolutely critical.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our relations with our closest neighbours, Indonesia and Malaysia, will always be of special importance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about the outcomes of the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat in January and how this would affect the trajectory of our bilateral relations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think you all know that Singapore and Indonesia are close partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Defence Cooperation Agreement will strengthen cooperation between our two armed forces.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It will provide clarity on the arrangements for the SAF's training in the Indonesian archipelagic and territorial waters and airspace, which is conducted with full respect for Indonesia's sovereignty, whilst preserving Singapore's rights under UNCLOS.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This set of mutually beneficial and durable agreements shows the strength and maturity of our bilateral relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It illustrates our commitment to resolving longstanding bilateral matters in an open and constructive manner for the long-term benefit of our peoples.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee and President Joko Widodo both expressed the desire to ratify and bring these agreements into force soon.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Lee and President Joko Widodo also had good discussions on new areas of collaboration, including green economy, renewable energy, human capital development.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we look forward to making progress on all these fronts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The key point is that we can steadily resolve all issues and we can open up new areas with win-win outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For Malaysia, I want to tell you that we have maintained our very close relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I would say, it has probably even been strengthened by our shared experience of COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Malaysia is our closest neighbour and bilateral engagements continued both formally and informally throughout this pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our Ministers have been communicating: WhatsApp, letters, phone calls, video calls.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And most importantly, at times of greatest need, we are available for each other.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And one thing which I want to cite is that we made sure our supply chains both ways never failed, even in the depths of the crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We were still able to facilitate the safe movement of goods, services and people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, trade in goods and services increased in 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We collaborated closely with Malaysia to restore connectivity, launch Vaccinated Travel Lanes (VTLs) for both land and air travel on 29 November 2021 and helped restore some – I say "some", because it is still a very small fraction – of the pre-pandemic flow of tourists and business people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also helped to reunite families on both sides of the Causeway and I know we all look forward to expanding cross-border travel progressively and safely, and hopefully, at some point, back to pre-pandemic levels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On ASEAN, let me just quickly say that Mr Henry Kwek asked about the concerns with Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Unfortunately, there has been no significant progress at all.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to work with the ASEAN Chair – Cambodia this year – as we did with Brunei last year, and, indeed, with our fellow ASEAN members to continue trying to promote, persuade, cajole, and reach a peaceful and durable resolution of the situation in Myanmar through the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Chairman, since MFA's establishment in 1965, our Mission has always been to uphold the independence and sovereignty of Singapore, to protect and advance the interests of Singaporeans, both at home and overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we must thus continue to invest in this effort of diplomacy, even as the Government tackles all the immediate challenges of the day.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Just as supply chains are moving from "Just-in-Time" to "Just-in-Case", for a small city-state like Singapore, we must always prepare for all possible scenarios.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is in our fundamental interest to ensure that our partners around the world have a stake in our continued peace and prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must never take our independence, sovereignty, peace and security for granted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to begin by following up on what Minister Vivian Balarishnan had just shared about our relations with our closest neighbours – Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong’s question on how we have engaged Malaysia amidst the pandemic is a pertinent one as our two countries are deeply intertwined.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Two years of living with COVID-19 have underscored the depth of our ties and the value of close cooperation for mutual benefit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The prolonged closure of our borders has thus had a profound impact on the people on both sides, with many families and relatives separated.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Given our interdependencies, the two governments have worked closely to overcome the challenges posed by COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We coordinated to ensure the sustainable movement of supplies, goods and services, and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Malaysia’s closest neighbour, Singapore always stands ready to do our part to help when needed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We contributed seed money to support the Singapore Red Cross’ disaster relief and recovery efforts following the floods in Kuala Lumpur and nine other Malaysian states in December 2021, as we had done in previous similar instances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are similarly very grateful for Malaysia's assistance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Recently, Malaysia helped to facilitate the departure of a Singaporean from Ukraine.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond our relations with the federal government, we have also maintained our ties with various Malaysian states.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have contributed medical supplies and vaccines, and shared our experiences on vaccine procurement and other areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The recent land VTL between Singapore and Malaysia has provided much relief to both Malaysians and Singaporeans as they are now able to meet their families again.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Looking ahead, we will continue our engagement of Malaysian leaders and officials across all levels while working towards the further expansion of cross-border travel and reinvigorating our economic ties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore and Indonesia enjoy strong and substantive relations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have been Indonesia’s largest foreign investor since 2014.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Bilateral Investment Treaty, which entered into force last year, will promote greater bilateral investment flows.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To further deepen our economic and people-to-people links, we are exploring new areas of cooperation, such as in the digital economy, the green economy and human capital development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also continued our close cooperation with the various regions across Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our economic engagements in Batam, Bintan and Karimun have progressed well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Its proximity to Singapore offers opportunities for Singapore-based companies to tap on Singapore and Indonesia's complementary tech ecosystems to support their digital needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This demonstrates Singapore and Indonesia’s mutual commitment to develop Batam as a "digital bridge" between us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Infrastructure Asia, which was set up by ESG and MAS, is also partnering the West Java provincial government to accelerate infrastructure projects focusing on urban transportation, waste management and water sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This partnership will increase the attractiveness of West Java’s infrastructure projects to international investors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, it allows Singapore-based companies to better access and participate in projects in West Java.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked how we have maintained our excellent relations with Brunei.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have always enjoyed a longstanding, special relationship with Brunei.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There remain strong links between our people, leaders and institutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan visited Brunei in March 2021, while Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean attended the Sultan’s 75th birthday celebrations in July 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also worked together to tackle the challenges of the pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In exchange, Brunei will provide the same quantity of vaccines back to Singapore at a later date.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain also asked about the highlights of Brunei’s ASEAN Chairmanship in 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore appreciated Brunei’s steady leadership in guiding ASEAN through a challenging year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Brunei led ASEAN’s efforts to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic, including utilising the COVID-19 ASEAN Response Fund to procure much-needed vaccines for our ASEAN Member States, and coordinated ASEAN’s response to address the situation in Myanmar.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked how our relations with the Gulf countries have developed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A number of our Ministers, including myself, have visited the Gulf in recent months.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I made a working visit to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Saudi Arabia and Qatar last October.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry Tan See Leng also co-chaired the inaugural Saudi-Singapore Joint Committee in December 2021, which we hope will catalyse greater trade and investment between Singapore and Saudi Arabia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In turn, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal Bin Farhan Al Saud visited Singapore in January 2022, his first to Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During his phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammad Bin Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud last month, Prime Minister Lee had welcomed the deepening of ties between our two countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to speak briefly in Malay, please.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Zhulkarnain had asked whether we can expect Haj to resume for Singapore pilgrims in 2022 since Umrah for international pilgrims has resumed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am glad that Singaporean Muslims have been able to travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, after being unable to do so for much of 2020 and 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to receiving more details on whether Haj 2022 will be open to international pilgrims and also an increase in our Haj quota.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I understand that Mr Alex Yam also wanted to know about developments in the Middle East, including the impact of the Abraham Accords.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While the geopolitical situation in the Middle East remains fluid, there have been some positive developments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Following the signing of the Abraham Accords, relations between Israel and the UAE, Bahrain and Morocco have advanced quickly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that the Abraham Accords will serve as a foundation for peace and stability in the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last May’s escalation of violence between Israel and Hamas in Gaza was their fifth major conflict in the last 15 years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We were saddened by the loss of civilian lives on both sides.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Nevertheless, the situation in Gaza is partly a manifestation of intra-Palestinian political rivalries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The West Bank is governed by the Palestinian Authority (PA) and controlled by the Fatah Party, while Hamas seized unilateral control of Gaza in 2007.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This political divide has persisted despite past attempts at forging a national unity government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Unlike Fatah, Hamas does not officially recognise Israel’s right to exist and believes in armed conflict.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore remains steadfast in our support for a negotiated two-state solution that allows Israelis and the Palestinians to live side-by-side in peace and security, consistent with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is the only viable option to achieve a durable, just and comprehensive solution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This training has continued online during the pandemic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also expanded the postgraduate scholarships for Palestinians to include Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) disciplines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At present, we have two Palestinian scholars in Singapore pursuing their postgraduate studies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I was happy to meet one of the students last week, who is pursuing a Master’s degree in International Relations at RSIS in NTU.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to doing more under the ETAP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For MFA, extending consular assistance to overseas Singaporeans remains our key priority.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, we must also continue to support global and regional efforts against COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, geopolitical flashpoints and major power rivalry and the implications for Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must continue to make decisions based on our national interests and fundamental principles, and to fight for these principles to be upheld.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, non-traditional security challenges, such as climate change and food security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore remains committed to working together with our partners, bilaterally as well as through multilateral fora, such as ASEAN, to address them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Fourth, maintaining good relations with our neighbours to promote peace and security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And fifth, upholding ASEAN's credibility to work towards a peaceful and durable resolution in Myanmar through the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, allow me to continue my speech in English, please.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Henry Kwek sought an update on our ties with other Southeast Asian countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We enjoy warm and friendly relations with our fellow ASEAN Member States, including Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Cambodia and Laos.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just last week, we welcomed Vietnamese President Nguyen Xuan Phuc for his State Visit to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to closely engage and pursue collaborative interests with our Southeast Asian partners, including the diversification of our food and energy options, as well as in emerging areas, such as digital economy and sustainable development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to be a steadfast friend during both good and trying times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN remains a cornerstone of Singapore’s foreign policy and we will continue to build up ASEAN’s resilience and responsiveness to future public health emergencies and support ASEAN’s post-pandemic recovery.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, the ASEAN (Travel) Corridor Arrangement Framework, when operationalised, will allow for the safe resumption of travel, both for business and leisure, within the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN also continues to serve as a vital regional architecture for external powers to engage ASEAN member states and one another.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are now discussing similar proposals by the US and India, and the US has invited ASEAN Leaders to an ASEAN-US Special Summit this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Given ASEAN’s importance, Mr Liang Eng Hwa’s query on Singapore’s role in maintaining ASEAN’s centrality, unity and credibility is apt.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In our capacity as ASEAN Smart Cities Network (ASCN) Shepherd, we also hope to work with Cambodia, ASEAN's current chair, to advance cooperation on Smart Cities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked if there are potential areas that Singapore can develop further in our relations with India.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We continue to have active engagements in the economic, security and people-to-people domains.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India has a vibrant and youthful population, a thriving tech sector, and its economy is well-positioned to strengthen in the years ahead.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India’s economic growth will benefit the rest of Asia, including Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As of 2020, there were 5,800 Singapore-based companies that either exported to or invested in India.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These include SMEs such as EnvironSens, which develops water toxicity monitoring technology, as well as another SME, Graymatics, a cloud-based video analytics service provider.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
